channel.description: Recent content in Career on Best of AI

item.title: Poised
item.description:
Poised is a communication coach for online meetings. During a call, the app runs privately on the user’s device, tracks how they speak, and shows real-time prompts such as slowing down or reducing filler words. After the call, it provides a summary and trends over time.

Practice features let users rehearse presentations or interviews and get analysis. It is designed for professionals, students, and non-native English speakers who want to improve how they come across.

item.title: Yoodli
item.description:
Yoodli is an AI speech coach. A user records themselves or practices with an AI role-play partner, and the tool analyzes delivery: filler words, speaking rate, pauses, and word choice, and gives a report with suggestions and trends over time.

Role-play scenarios cover interviews, sales calls, and presentations, where an AI plays the other party and responds. Organizations use Yoodli for sales and leadership training, with private practice that removes the embarrassment of rehearsing in front of others.

item.title: Enhancv
item.description:
Enhancv guides people through writing a resume. A user chooses a template, fills in experience, and gets prompts and suggestions on wording, such as adding numbers to show results and avoiding vague phrases. A content analyzer scores the draft and points out weak areas.

Templates are designed to be readable by applicant tracking systems, and sections can be customized for different roles. Additional tools include cover letter help, a resume checker, and a personal website option. AI features suggest bullet points and rewrite text, which can save time when starting from scratch.

item.title: Huntr
item.description:
Huntr helps people stay organized during a job hunt. Users save job postings with a browser extension, move them across stages as they apply and interview, and attach notes, contacts, and documents to each one. Reminders prompt follow-ups so opportunities do not slip.

AI features assist with the writing. They can tailor a resume and cover letter to a posting, suggest keywords, and help prepare for interviews. A resume builder and job board aggregator add to the toolset, and career coaches use Huntr to track clients.

item.title: Jobscan
item.description:
Jobscan helps people tailor resumes to individual jobs. A user pastes in a resume and a job posting, and Jobscan reports a match score, lists keywords and skills from the posting that are missing or underused, and points out formatting problems that could trip up automated parsers.

Additional tools include a LinkedIn optimization feature, cover letter checks, and AI that suggests wording and rewrites sections. A job tracker helps organize applications. The service is popular with career coaches and people applying to large companies that use applicant tracking systems.

item.title: Teal
item.description:
Teal helps people manage a job hunt. A Chrome extension saves postings from job boards to a tracker with stages and notes, and tools remind users to follow up. A resume builder creates versions tailored to each posting, with suggestions for keywords and phrasing.

AI features help write bullet points, summaries, and cover letters, and a match score shows how well a resume fits a job. Teal also offers career resources and tools for networking and LinkedIn.

item.title: Glassdoor
item.description:
Glassdoor made workplace information public. Employees write anonymous reviews of their employers, covering culture, management, pay, and benefits, and share salary data and the questions they were asked in interviews. Job seekers use it to research a company before applying or accepting an offer, and to check whether an offer is in line with what others earn in similar roles.

The site also runs a job board and tools for employers. Companies can respond to reviews, post jobs, and promote their employer brand, while job seekers can search listings, set alerts, and apply. AI features appear in job recommendations and in summaries of reviews and salary information. Many of the platform’s operations have been merged with Indeed, its sister site, and Glassdoor is now legally part of Indeed, though the brand and reviews continue.

item.title: Indeed
item.description:
Indeed started as a search engine for job listings, pulling postings from company career pages and other boards into one place. Job seekers search by title and location, set alerts, upload a resume, and apply directly, often in a few clicks. The site also provides salary estimates, company information, and reviews, and Indeed is now closely tied to Glassdoor, which is part of the same company.

For employers, it is a major source of applicants. Companies post jobs for free or pay to sponsor them for more visibility, and tools help with screening questions, scheduling interviews, and messaging candidates. AI features match job seekers to relevant roles and recommend candidates to employers, summarize job requirements, and increasingly assist with resume improvement and hiring workflows. Recruiters search a resume database, with paid access to some functions.

item.title: Kickresume
item.description:
Kickresume helps people create resumes quickly. You choose a template, enter your experience, and the builder arranges everything in a clean layout. A library of professionally designed templates covers different industries and styles, and the exports are designed to be readable by applicant tracking systems, which scan resumes before a human sees them. It also builds cover letters, personal websites, and portfolios.

AI assists with the writing. The AI resume writer can generate summaries and bullet points from your role and achievements, tailor a resume for a specific job description, and write a cover letter. A resume checker evaluates structure, keywords, and clarity and suggests improvements, and extra tools help with interview practice and job tracking. The AI features speed up drafting but can produce generic language.

item.title: LinkedIn
item.description:
LinkedIn is the main place for professional identity online. Members create profiles that work as living resumes, connect with colleagues and contacts, follow companies, and share posts and articles. It is also a major channel for hiring and job hunting, with job listings, recruiter messaging, and tools that show how you compare with other applicants. Companies maintain pages and advertise to professional audiences.

AI features run through the product. Job search can be done in plain language, writing assistance helps draft posts and profile sections, and an AI hiring assistant helps recruiters find and screen candidates. Premium subscriptions add insights, more messages, and learning courses through LinkedIn Learning. Skills assessments, recommendations, and endorsements are used to signal ability. The feed is ranked by algorithms that favor engagement.

item.title: Resume.io
item.description:
Resume.io helps job seekers create a polished resume quickly. You choose a template, fill in your experience, education, and skills in a guided form, and see the layout update. The templates are designed to be clean and readable by applicant tracking systems, and you can adjust colors and fonts, reorder sections, and download the result as a PDF. Cover letter and CV builders follow the same approach.

AI features help with the hard part, which is the wording. The assistant suggests bullet points for a job title, drafts a professional summary, and can tailor a resume to a job description. A resume checker highlights weaknesses, and a job tracker helps manage applications. The tool also provides guides and examples for different professions.

item.title: Rezi
item.description:
Rezi focuses on a specific worry: that automated screening software will reject a resume before a person reads it. The builder uses a simple, single-column layout and standard section names that parsing software reads reliably. As you write, a score shows how well the resume matches ATS best practices, with checks on length, formatting, action verbs, and keywords from a target job posting.

AI helps with content. It can generate bullet points from a role and tasks, rewrite weak phrases into stronger ones, and tailor a resume to a job description. It also drafts cover letters and has features for tracking applications and tuning your LinkedIn profile. The interface is plain, with less design flair than many competitors, which is intentional.

item.title: Zety
item.description: Zety walks job seekers through making a resume. You choose a template, answer prompts about your experience and education, and see a preview that updates as you type. The builder suggests wording for job duties and skills, which is helpful if you struggle with the phrasing, and it formats everything cleanly for PDF or Word download. It also builds cover letters and offers a library of guides and examples for different industries.

item.title: ZipRecruiter
item.description:
ZipRecruiter works on both sides of hiring. An employer writes a job once, and ZipRecruiter posts it across a network of job boards and sends it to potential candidates through email and notifications. Job seekers create a profile or upload a resume, browse listings, set alerts, and apply with a click, and the platform recommends jobs based on their interests and activity.

Matching technology is central. The system learns from employer and candidate behavior to recommend candidates to employers and jobs to seekers, and employers can invite candidates to apply. Tools help screen applicants, schedule interviews, and communicate in one place. AI features assist with writing job descriptions and surfacing strong matches, and an employer dashboard tracks responses.

item.title: Jobbyo
item.description:
Jobbyo automates the repetitive parts of looking for work. A user uploads a resume and states the roles they want, and the agent searches for matching openings, fills in applications, and tracks responses. The idea is to apply to many more jobs than a person could by hand.

Volume is not the same as success. Hiring teams complain about floods of automated applications, and many applicant tracking systems filter them, so tailored applications to well-chosen roles usually work better. Some employers also restrict automated submissions in their terms.

item.title: JobGPT
item.description:
JobGPT covers much of the job application workflow. It searches for postings that match a profile, adjusts the resume’s wording to fit each description, drafts a cover letter, and fills in application forms. Users review results and track their applications.

The appeal is time saved on repetitive forms. The risk is quality: automatically generated materials can be generic or inaccurate, and recruiters can spot copy-paste applications. Tailoring should stay truthful, and every application deserves a quick review before it goes out.

item.title: Reztune
item.description:
Reztune helps job seekers customize applications. A user uploads a resume and pastes a job posting, and the AI rewrites sections to match the role, emphasizing relevant skills and adjusting wording to align with terms in the posting.

Tailoring takes time to do by hand, and tools like this make it faster, which appeals to people applying to many jobs. The risk is overstating experience or producing generic phrasing, so users should review every line for accuracy.
